"Adtalem’s $750 Million Share Repurchase Signals Confidence and Undervaluation"
Check it out..Its free!!
👇
Had lunch with a couple of investor friends this week and one of them was talking about taking Waymos, while we ordered food via QR code with almost no staff interaction. In an AI-driven world that’s reimagining labor, career-focused education is back in the spotlight.
For-profit education has a troubled history (Corinthian Colleges, ITT Tech, and the 2011 regulatory crackdown). But one player didn't fold - it pivoted. 
 Adtalem Global Education  $ATGE, the former DeVry that pivoted into healthcare 
👩‍⚕️
👨‍⚕️
Formerly DeVry University, the company rebranded in 2017, sold off its legacy assets, and went all-in on the one sector AI can't easily replace: Healthcare. 
🩺
Here is the breakdown of the situation, the opportunity, and the risks. 
👇
📊
 The Snapshot
Ticker: $ATGE
Price: ~$103.62
Market Cap: $3.73B
Enterprise Value: $4.24B
Valuation: ~12.2x Forward P/E (Cheap vs. Peers)
Graduates: 29,000 students this year.
Focus: ~90% of degrees are in healthcare-related professions.
Core Assets: Chamberlain University (Nursing) & Walden University.
Growth: Chamberlain & Walden have posted average quarterly enrollment gains of 9% and 13.5% respectively.
The Tailwind: A Massive Labor Shortage
The U.S. faces a severe healthcare crisis. It needs 1.2 million+ new registered nurses(RN's) by 2030 to replace retirees. Physician and mental health professional shortages are worsening.
Unlike elite med schools ($95k/year), Adtalem offers a more accessible path ($60k-$70k), directly feeding the workforce.
💰
 The Capital Allocation Machine
Management is aggressively returning cash to shareholders.
Buybacks: Since Feb 2022, they’ve repurchased 17.2M shares (a 30% reduction in share count).
New Authorization: Just approved a $750M buyback program (~21% of market cap).
Debt: Reduced by $1.1B since the Walden acquisition.
📉
 The Opportunity (The Dip)
Despite strong results, the stock sold off 31% recently due to conservative guidance for FY2026 (projecting 6-8.5% growth vs. last year's 13%).
The Signal: Insiders started buying.
Directors stepped in to purchase shares in the $25-$40 range in 2021-22, and they are buying again post-dip.
Valuation
It still trades around 12x forward earnings despite a massive nurse/physician shortage tailwind which and 15 straight top- and bottom-line beats. This is at a discount to most peers like $UTI and $LINC 
📈
.
The Risks:
The biggest risk for any education stock is the government. Adtalem relies heavily on federal financial aid (Title IV).
The Rules: They must adhere to strict regulations like the "90/10 Rule" (no more than 90% of revenue from gov funds) and "Gainful Employment" (proving students actually get jobs).
Good News: Their regulatory standing has improved, with letter of credit requirements dropping from 20% -> 10%, freeing up more cash.
🧠
 Final Thoughts
Adtalem has cleaned up its balance sheet, focused its mission, and is buying back its own stock hand-over-fist. While the conservative guidance is a short-term dampener, the long-term trend of healthcare demand + aggressive capital returns makes this a turnaround story worth watching
👀

title: Heavy truck sales are a leading indicator of the l...
content:
Heavy truck sales are a leading indicator of the labor market because they reveal what businesses actually believe about the future. 
When trucking companies and logistics operators are optimistic, they buy trucks, it's a capital investment that signals confidence in handling more volume. 
When they're uncertain, truck purchases are one of the first expenses they cut. 
It's a direct window into business sentiment that often shows up in employment decisions months later.
Truck sales have dropped to 5.1 million units over the last 12 months, the lowest since 2020, and outside the pandemic period, you'd have to go back eight years to find this weakness. 
The decline of roughly 1.1 million units over the past 18 months represents a meaningful shift in how business leaders are thinking about demand and capacity.
The historical relationship is consistent and notable, virtually every time truck sales have peaked and declined in past economic cycles, unemployment has risen roughly six months later. 
If this pattern holds, the unemployment rate could rise by at least one percentage point over the next six months. 
For context, if unemployment is currently around 4%, that would push it toward 5%, a noticeable shift that signals the labor market is beginning to cool and business confidence is declining.
The US unemployment rate is likely heading higher:
US heavy truck sales are down to 5.1 million over the last 12 months, the lowest since 2020.
Outside the pandemic, this is the lowest level in 8 years.
Annual truck sales have declined by ~1.1 million over the last 18 months.
In previous economic cycles, this has been a leading indicator of higher unemployment.
This suggests that the unemployment rate may rise by at least 1.0 percentage point over the next 6 months.
Downside pressure on the labor market is building. 
-

title: Silver just hit $70 per ounce for the first time i...
content:
Silver just hit $70 per ounce for the first time in history, up roughly 144% this year alone. 
That's an absolutely massive move when you consider silver started 2025 around $29, completely shattering the previous all time record from 1980.​
Silver markets have been running deficits for five straight years, meaning we're using more than we're producing. 
Industrial demand is exploding from solar panels, electric vehicles, and AI data centers, all hungry for silver's conductive properties. 
As clean energy and AI infrastructure scale globally, that demand stays strong.​
Add in the monetary story, expectations of Fed rate cuts in 2026 are pushing investors out of dollars and into hard assets like precious metals. 
A weaker dollar also makes silver cheaper for international buyers, amplifying demand further. 
Geopolitical uncertainty is treating silver as a safe haven asset, similar to gold but with more upside potential since it hasn't gotten as much institutional attention historically.​
Retail investors are taking physical possession of silver at record rates, pulling real supply off the market and creating additional price pressure. 
Even Russia announced plans to buy $535 million worth over the next few years, the first central bank explicitly targeting silver during this rally.
